text: Summary of the issue The selection logic for HLS external audio tracks in parse_variant_playlist was only matching items from --hls-audio-select against language codes (LANGUAGE attribute) or recognized language names via pycountry (converted to Language objects). It did not consider the NAME attribute of the #EXT-X-MEDIA entries directly. This caused failures when users passed localized or arbitrary audio track names (like “TV Ton”, “Originalton”, “Deutsch”) that are not recognized by pycountry, leading to only a single default track being selected instead of the specified ones. What I changed I updated the audio selection logic in src/streamlink/stream/hls/hls.py to also match hls-audio-select input items against the HLS media’s NAME attribute, case-insensitively. Specifically, I added an additional condition: - When an item in hls-audio-select is not a recognized language (ie, it ends up in audio_select_codes), it’s now compared against media.name.strip().lower() for equality, and will be selected if it matches. This preserves existing behavior for: - "*" wildcard - language codes (eg. "en", "de", "es", etc.) - recognized language names (eg. "English", "Spanish", etc., via pycountry) and extends it to direct matching against the NAME attribute (eg. "Deutsch", "Français", "Español", "TV Ton", "Originalton"). Reproduction tests To validate the fix, I added a new test resource and test case: - tests/resources/hls/test_media_language_names.m3u8 Contains audio tracks with names "Deutsch", "Français", "Español" mapped to URIs de.m3u8, fr.m3u8, es.m3u8. - tests/stream/hls/test_hls.py in TestHlsExtAudio Added test_multiple_names which sets --hls-audio-select to ["Deutsch", "Français", "Español"] and asserts that the resulting MuxedHLSStream substreams include the correct audio URIs. I also ensured existing tests for language names (like "English" and "spanish") still work as before. Code changes File: src/streamlink/stream/hls/hls.py In HLSStream.parse_variant_playlist(), I changed the “preferred_audio” selection logic: Old: - Only matched language codes or parsed Language instances, plus locale equivalence fallback New: - Added comparison against media.name (case-insensitive) for items in audio_select_codes that are not recognized language codes Snippet of the updated selection condition: - or ( media.name is not None and media.name.strip().lower() in audio_select_codes ) Result of running tests - Ran the full test suite: 6619 passed, 30 skipped - Ran the new test specifically: TestHlsExtAudio::test_multiple_names passed - No regressions observed How this addresses your examples - ZDF: --hls-audio-select "TV Ton,Originalton" Now both names will be matched directly against the NAME field in the M3U8, and both audio tracks will be included. - ARD: --hls-audio-select "Deutsch,Original" “Deutsch” is a localized name and not recognized by pycountry as a language; after the fix, it’s matched by NAME. “Original” is also a NAME attribute and will be included. - EBS: --hls-audio-select "English,Français,Deutsch,Español" This now matches by NAME as well, so it will work similarly to using language codes ("en,fr,de,es"). Notes - Matching is equality-based and case-insensitive on the NAME attribute as entered. - Language code matching is unchanged. - Wildcard "*" is unchanged. - Locale fallback behavior remains unchanged. Next steps If you want, I can refine matching rules further (eg. partial matches or normalization beyond lowercasing), but the current fix restores the previous expected behavior of name-based selection without affecting code-based selection. I have not committed these changes.
